title: Dengue deaths reach 478 as 1,900 more are admitted
excerpt: All four deaths in the 24 hours to 8am on 11 November were in Dhaka division. More than 6,000 patients remain in hospital.
content:
Four people died of dengue and 1,900 were admitted to hospital in the 24 hours to 8am on Wednesday, 11 November, according to Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS) data reported by The Business Standard and The Daily Star. All four deaths were in Dhaka division.

The numbers

  • Deaths this year: 478.
  • Admissions this year: 155,668, of whom 149,123 have recovered.
  • In hospital now: 6,067, down from 6,136 a day earlier, as 1,965 patients were discharged.
  • Trend: daily admissions over the last three bulletins were 2,260, 1,595 and 1,900. Deaths were five, eight and four.

Why it matters

Admissions are still close to 2,000 a day in mid-November, and Dhaka division accounts for most deaths. Doctors are also seeing children with measles and dengue at the same time. NGOs with urban health, WASH and volunteer programmes can keep up breeding-site clean-ups and push early referral for fever.

What to watch

Whether daily admissions drop below 1,500 as temperatures fall later in November.
